dervis-irab:22-26.t:
* I'rab:
(وَخَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ) You may make the speech conjoined to what preceded, so that it serves as a proof of the denial of equality between the two groups, or you may make it resumptive (istiʾnāf), introduced for this purpose. (وخلق الله السموات): a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (والأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); and (بالحق) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent or of the object. (وَلِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal; (تجزى) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) أن after the causal lām. The speech is conjoined to His words (بالحق), because both the bāʾ and the lām can express cause, so the creation is given the recompense as its cause. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that it be conjoined to an omitted cause, its implied form being "so that He may show by it His power, and so that every soul may be recompensed". Ibn ʿAṭiyya chose that it be the lām of consequence or outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba / al-ṣayrūra), i.e. and the matter came to be such that by them some people were guided and by them others went astray — and this is not far-fetched. The wāw is of ḥāl; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (لا يظلمون) is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ هَواهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ) The hamza is of interrogation intended as a command, i.e. "inform me". (رأيت) is a verb and its agent; (من) is the first object of (رأيت), and the second is omitted, its implied form being "guided" (مهتديا). The clause (اتخذ) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (إلهه) is the first object of (اتخذ) and (هواه) its second object. (أضله الله): a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. (على علم) is a ḥāl of the object, and this is preferable to making it a ḥāl of the agent, as al-Jalāl parsed it; the meaning is: Allah led him astray while he knew the truth, because the intensification in this is greater and the censure and condemnation of him more. (وَخَتَمَ عَلى سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَجَعَلَ عَلى بَصَرِهِ غِشاوَةً) Conjoined to what preceded; the discussion of this verse has already been given in al-Baqara. (فَمَنْ يَهْدِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ اللَّهِ أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun in the sense of negation, i.e. no one guides him, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يهديه) is the khabar; and (من بعد الله) are attached to (يهديه). The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted, implied clause, i.e. "do you persist in error?"; (لا) is negating, and (تذكرون) is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped. (وَقالُوا: ما هِيَ إِلَّا حَياتُنَا الدُّنْيا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيا وَما يُهْلِكُنا إِلَّا الدَّهْرُ) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to refute their claims, since they used to claim that the perishing of souls depends on the passing of days and nights — more of this discussion will come in the section on Benefits. (ما) is negating; (هي) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (حياتنا) is a mubtadaʾ and (الدنيا) a khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; (الدنيا) is ordinarily parsed as an adjective of (حياتنا), which is the khabar of (هي)]. The clause (نموت) is resumptive, introduced to present more of their corrupt beliefs, and the clause (نحيا) is conjoined to it. The wāw is of ḥāl; (ما) is negating; (يهلكنا) is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (الدهر) is the agent of (يهلكنا). (وَما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (ما) is negating; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (بذلك) are attached to (علم); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (علم) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (إن) is negating, (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and the clause (يظنون) is their khabar. (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ ما كانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا ائْتُوا بِآبائِنا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (تتلى) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and it is passive; (عليهم) are attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (بيّنات) is a ḥāl, i.e. clear in their indication. (ما) is negating; (كان) is a defective past verb; (حجتهم) is the fronted khabar of (كان); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (أن قالوا): أن and what it governs are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of (كان); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ائتوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; (بآبائنا) are attached to (ائتوا); and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then bring them"; (صادقين) is the khabar of (كنتم). (قُلِ اللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) (قل) is an imperative verb; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يحييكم) its khabar; (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay, pointing to the interval separating life and death; (يميتكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and an object; (ثم) is a conjunction as before; (يجمعكم) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, and the kāf is the object; (إلى يوم القيامة) are attached to (يجمعكم). (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (ريب) is its noun and (فيه) its khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl of (يوم القيامة). (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يعلمون) is its khabar.

* Benefits:
Al-dahr (time) in the language is the duration of the world's existence, from "dahrahum amrun", i.e. time struck them with it. In al-Qāmūs: «dahrahum amrun, on the pattern of manaʿa: something hateful befell them; and they are madhūrun bihim and madhūrūn». It was the custom of the Arabs, when misfortune struck them, to ascribe it to time (al-dahr), believing that it is what does whatever it wills; and you see their poetry speaking out in complaint against time, so that this is found even in the poetry of Muslims. Ibn Durayd said in his Maqṣūra:
يا دهر إن لم تك عتبى فاتئد ... في إروادك والعتبى سوا
(O Time, if there is to be no making amends, then go gently in your pace — and making amends is the same.)
Abū al-ʿAlāʾ refuted the views of the Dahriyya (materialists) in his Luzūmiyyāt, saying:
ودان أناس بالجزاء وكونه ... وقال رجال إنما أنتم بقل
(Some people believed in recompense and its coming to pass, while other men said: you are nothing but herbage.)
This is a reply to the Dahriyya, who say that the world is eternal by nature, has always been so, and did not come into being through the act of an originator, and that people are like plants: they sprout and return through death to dry stubble. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said, refuting Ibn al-Rāwandī and his book al-Tāj, in Risālat al-Ghufrān, among what he said: «As for Ibn al-Rāwandī, he was not guided to what is right; and as for his Crown (Tāj), it is not fit to be even a sandal. Is his Crown anything but as the soothsayer woman said: "Uff and tuff, a sock and a slipper"?» And the Prophet ﷺ said: «Do not revile time, for Allah is time», i.e. because He, the Exalted, is the One who does whatever He wills, not time. The ḥadīth was narrated by al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others from Abū Hurayra.

dervis-irab:27-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جاثِيَةً) One says: jathā ʿalā rukbatayhi juthuwwan (he knelt on his knees); I saw him kneeling (jāthiyan) before him, and I saw them kneeling (juthiyyan) at his side. In the ḥadīth: «I shall be the first to kneel for the dispute before Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection». They knelt facing one another on their knees (tajāthaw), and he knelt facing his opponent (ajāthā khaṣmahu mujāthātan); and so-and-so became a juthwa (heap) of earth. Ṭarafa said:
ترى جثوتين من تراب عليهما ... صفائح صمّ من صفيح منضّد
(You see two heaps of earth upon which lie hard slabs, from stacked slabs.)
That is: I see the grave of the miser and of the generous man as two mounds of earth with broad hard stones upon them, among graves upon which broad stones have been stacked. The wording of al-Qurṭubī: «There are five interpretations of al-jāthiya. The first: Mujāhid said: crouching ready (mustawfiza); Sufyān said: the one crouching ready is the one of whom nothing touches the ground but his knees and the tips of his fingers; al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: and that is at the Reckoning. The second: gathered together, said by Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is, you see the people of every religion gathered together. The third: set apart, said by ʿIkrima. The fourth: humbled, in the dialect of Quraysh. The fifth: kneeling on the knees, said by al-Ḥasan. Al-juthuww is sitting on the knees; one says jathā ʿalā rukbatayhi yajthū and yajthī, juthuwwan and juthiyyan, on the pattern fuʿūl in both; this has already been discussed in Maryam. The origin of al-juthwa is a group of anything. Then it was said that it is specific to the disbelievers, said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām; and it was said that it is general for the believer and the disbeliever, awaiting the Reckoning. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh that the Prophet ﷺ said: It is as though I see you kneeling on your knees short of Hell.» Further, it has been read jādhiya, with dhāl; and al-judhuww is more of a crouching-ready posture than al-juthuww, because the jādhī is the one who sits on the tips of his toes.
(نَسْتَنْسِخُ) That is, We have the angels write down your deeds. In al-Asās:
«I copied (nasakhtu) my book from so-and-so's book, intasakhtuhu and istansakhtuhu, with the same meaning; and istinsākh can mean having something written (istiktāb): "Indeed We were having written down (nastansikhu)". This is an old copy (nuskha) and old copies (nusakh).» The meaning is: We command the angels to copy what you used to do and to record it; so what is meant by naskh here is not cancelling one thing and putting another in its place.

* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) Resumptive speech, introduced to generalise the power after specifying it with giving life, causing death and gathering, because the meaning of owner is one who disposes of what he owns as he wills. (لله) is a fronted khabar (predicate), and (ملك السموات والأرض) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَخْسَرُ الْمُبْطِلُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb attached to (يخسر); the clause (تقوم الساعة) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, and it is a badal (substitute) of (يوم تقوم); the tanwīn in (يومئذ) is a tanwīn of compensation for a clause, i.e. "the day the Hour is established". It was also said that what governs (ويوم تقوم) is what (الملك) indicates; they said: because the heaven and the earth will be changed, so it is as though it were said "and to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and the dominion on the Day of Resurrection"; on this view (يومئذ) is accusative by (يخسر). (يخسر المبطلون): a verb and its fāʿil (agent). (وَتَرى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جاثِيَةً، كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعى إِلى كِتابِهَا) The wāw is a conjunction; (ترى) is an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) agent, its implied form being "you"; (كل أمة) is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) if the seeing is cognitive, but the context of the speech favours its being visual; (جاثية) is a second object on the first view and a ḥāl (circumstantial) on the second. (كل أمة) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (تدعى إلى كتابها) is the khabar. (الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (تجزون); (تجزون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) is the second object of (تجزون); and the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. it will be said to them: "Today you are recompensed". (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تعملون) is its khabar; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (هذا كِتابُنا يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ) (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ, (كتابنا) a khabar, and the clause (ينطق) a second khabar or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. It is also permissible for (كتابنا) to be a badal of (هذا), with the clause (ينطق) as the khabar of (هذا). (بالحق) is a ḥāl, and (عليكم) are attached to (ينطق). The meaning of the book's speaking will come in the section on Rhetoric. (إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنْسِخُ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (إن) and its noun; the clause (كنّا) is the khabar of (إنّا); the clause (نستنسخ) is the khabar of (كنّا); (ما) is a direct object; the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila of (ما); and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم). (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أما) is a particle of condition and of detailing the summary understood from His words (ينطق عليكم بالحق) or from (تجزون); (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا). (فيدخلهم): the fāʾ links the apodosis of (أما), and the clause (يدخلهم ربهم في رحمته) is the khabar of (الذين). (ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ) Its i'rab has been given many times. (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آياتِي تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; and the apodosis of (أما) is omitted, its implied form being "then it will be said to them". The hamza is of interrogation, and the fāʾ is conjoined to the omitted apodosis; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (تكن) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); the meaning is "did not My messengers come to you, and were not…". (آياتي) is the noun of (تكن), and the clause (تتلى عليكم) is its khabar. (فَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْماً مُجْرِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (استكبرتم) is a verb and its agent; (كنتم): (كان) and its noun; (قوما) is its khabar, and (مجرمين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قوما).

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His words «هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق» there is an implicit metaphor: the book is likened to a witness who delivers his testimony truthfully; the thing to which it is likened is omitted, and one of its concomitants — speaking the testimony — is borrowed for it.
2- In His words «فيدخلهم في رحمته» there is a synecdochic trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is that of the occupant (al-ḥāliyya), i.e. into His Garden; because a person does not dwell in mercy, since it is an abstract notion; he dwells only in its place. So using "mercy" for its place is a trope in which the occupant is mentioned and the place is meant, and its relation is that of the occupant.

dervis-irab:32-37.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَالسَّاعَةُ لا رَيْبَ فِيها قُلْتُمْ ما نَدْرِي مَا السَّاعَةُ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what preceded because it is part of what is said to them. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; (قيل) is a passive past verb, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (إن) with its noun and khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (الساعة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (لا ريب فيها) is its khabar. It was also said that (الساعة) is conjoined to the position of (إن) and its noun together, because إن and its noun have a position, namely nominative by being the subject. (والساعة) was also read in the accusative, conjoined to (الوعد). The clause [ما الساعة] is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of (ندري), because the verb is suspended (ʿulliqat) by the interrogative. The clause (قلتم) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ما) is negating; (ندري) is a nominative imperfect verb; (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (الساعة) is its khabar. (إِنْ نَظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّا وَما نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ) (إن) is negating; (نظن) is a nominative imperfect verb; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (ظنا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). This construction is one of the difficulties around which the grammarians and exegetes have hummed at length; we shall give you more on it in the section on Benefits. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating mā; (نحن) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (مستيقنين) is genitive by the bāʾ in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ما). (وَبَدا لَهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ ما عَمِلُوا وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) The wāw is resumptive; (بدا) is a past verb; (لهم) are attached to (بدا); (سيئات) is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (حاق بهم) is conjoined to (بدا لهم); (ما) is the agent of (حاق); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; (به) are attached to (يستهزئون); and the clause (يستهزئون) is the khabar of (كانوا). (وَقِيلَ الْيَوْمَ نَنْساكُمْ كَما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا) The wāw is a conjunction; (قيل) is a passive past verb; (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (ننساكم); (كما) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); (نسيتم) is a verb and its agent; (لقاء يومكم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The adverb has been used broadly, so that what occurs in it is annexed to it, in the manner of His words "the plotting of the night" (makr al-layl). (هذا) is a naʿt of (يومكم) or a badal (substitute) of it. (وَمَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (مأواكم) is a fronted khabar and (النار) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the reverse is permissible. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition; and (ناصرين) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (ذلِكُمْ بِأَنَّكُمُ اتَّخَذْتُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ هُزُواً) (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the great punishment prepared for them. (بأنكم): أن and what is in its domain are in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of (ذلك). (أن) and its noun, and the clause (اتخذتم) is its khabar; (آيات الله) is the first object of (اتخذتم), and (هزوا) is the second object of (اتخذتم). (وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا) The wāw is a conjunction; (غرّتكم) is a past verb and a fronted direct object; (الحياة) is a postponed agent, and (الدنيا) is a naʿt of (الحياة). (فَالْيَوْمَ لا يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْها وَلا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (يخرجون); (لا) is negating; (يخرجون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; (منها) are attached to (يخرجون). (ولا) is conjoined to what preceded; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يستعتبون) is the khabar. (فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَرَبِّ الْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (لله) is a fronted khabar and (الحمد) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (رب السموات) is a badal or naʿt of (لله), and likewise what follows it. (وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِياءُ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (له) is a fronted khabar and (الكبرياء) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الكبرياء), and it may be attached to the [notion of] being established to which the first adverbial phrase is attached; some chose that it be attached to (الكبرياء) itself, because it is a maṣdar. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, and (العزيز الحكيم) are two khabars of it.

* Rhetoric:
1- The synecdochic trope (al-majāz al-mursal) or the implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His words «وقيل اليوم ننساكم» etc. there is a majāz mursal whose relation is causality, because forgetting is the cause of leaving; when a thing is forgotten it is left and entirely neglected. Some said: it is also permissible to regard the pronoun of address as containing a metaphor by allusion (istiʿāra bi-l-kināya), likening them to a forgotten thing in their being left in the punishment and no heed being paid to them, with the attribution of forgetting being the indicator (qarīna) of the metaphor.
2- The shift of person (al-iltifāt): this is in His words «فاليوم لا يخرجون منها»; He shifted from address to the third person when He reached this state to which they had come, for they deserve to be dropped from the rank of being addressed, out of contempt and disdain for them.

* Benefits:
We pointed to the difficulty arising in His words, Exalted is He, «إن نظن إلا ظنا», because the emphatic maṣdar may not occur as an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); one does not say "I did not strike except a striking", since it has no benefit, being equivalent to saying "I did not strike except I struck". It is established among the grammarians that the governing word may be emptied for whatever follows it of all the governed elements except the absolute object; so one does not say "I did not think except a thinking", because the locus of negation and affirmation — namely thinking — is one and the same, whereas restriction is conceivable only when their loci differ. The following is what the grammarians said:
Al-Mubarrad said: its origin is "we are nothing but thinking a thinking" (in naḥnu illā naẓunnu ẓannan). He means that the locus of negation is omitted, namely the speaker's being engaged in some act or other; that is the locus of negation, and the locus of affirmation is his thinking a thinking. So the word (إلا), though placed later in the wording, is placed earlier in the implied structure. The import of the restriction is the affirmation of conjecture for themselves and the negation of everything other than it; among everything other than it is certainty, and it is what is intended to be negated; but He negated everything other than conjecture absolutely, for emphasis in negating certainty, and for that reason it was reinforced by His words (وما نحن بمستيقنين).
As for Abū Ḥayyān, he interpreted it as the omission of an adjective of the maṣdar, so that it becomes specifying rather than emphatic, its implied form being "except a weak conjecture"; or as (نظن) being made to carry the meaning of "we believe" (naʿtaqidu), so that (ظنا) is a direct object.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the meaning of His words (إن نظن إلا ظنا)? I say: its origin is "we think a thinking", and its meaning is the affirmation of conjecture together with the negation of everything else; and the negation of everything other than conjecture was further emphasised by His words: (وما نحن بمستيقنين).»
Abū Ḥayyān rebutted al-Zamakhsharī as is his habit, saying: «This is the speech of one who has no awareness of the grammatical rule that emptying [for the exception] occurs with all the governed elements — agent, object and others — except the emphatic maṣdar, for it does not occur with it.»
As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he said: «Its implied form is "we are nothing but thinking a thinking", so (إلا) has been postponed; were it not for this implied form, the meaning would be "we do not think except a thinking". It was also said that it is in its proper place, because (نظن) may have the meaning of knowledge and of doubt, so doubt was excepted, i.e. we have no belief except doubt.»

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(حم تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ): the discussion of the openings of the sūras has already preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it. تنزيل الكتاب is the subject and من الله its predicate; العزيز الحكيم are two adjectives of الله. It is also possible to parse تنزيل as the predicate of an omitted subject, with من الله attached to it.
(إِنَّ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآياتٍ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): إن is a particle resembling the verb; في السموات is a fronted predicate; the lām is for emphasis; آيات is the noun of أن; وللمؤمنين is an adjective of آيات.
(وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ وَما يَبُثُّ مِنْ دابَّةٍ آياتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ وَاخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وَما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِنْ رِزْقٍ فَأَحْيا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّياحِ آياتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; وفي خلقكم is a fronted predicate; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is a relative noun conjoined to خلقكم; the clause يبث is the ṣila; من دابة is attached to يبث or to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "He disperses it, being of the beasts"; آيات is a postponed subject; ولقوم is an adjective of آيات; the clause يوقنون is an adjective of قوم. واختلاف is also conjoined to خلقكم, «[Translator's note: the source text here reads "منزل تنزيله من أنه متعلق بمحذوف خبر مقدم", which is evidently garbled; it appears to mean that the phrase is attached to an omitted fronted predicate. Translated as written.]» ما is conjoined to اختلاف; أنزل الله is a verb and agent, and the clause is the ṣila of ما; من رزق is a ḥāl or is attached to أنزل; فأحيا is conjoined to أنزل; به is attached to أحيا; الأرض is the direct object; وتصريف الرياح is conjoined to اختلاف; آيات is a postponed subject; ولقوم is an adjective; the clause يعقلون is an adjective of قوم. It is useful to cite here the wording of al-Zamakhsharī, for he fully covered the readings in these two verses. He said: "«آيات لقوم يوقنون» was also read with accusative and with nominative, according to your saying 'Zayd is in the house and ʿAmr in the market' or 'and ʿAmr is in the market'. As for His saying «آيات لقوم يعقلون», it is conjoining upon two governors, whether you read it accusative or nominative. The two governors, if you read accusative, are إن and في; the wāw was made to stand in their place, so it acted with genitive in اختلاف الليل والنهار and accusative in آيات. If you read nominative, the two governors are inception (ibtidāʾ) and في, which acted with nominative in آيات and genitive in اختلاف. Ibn Masʿūd read: وفي اختلاف الليل والنهار. If you say: conjoining upon two governors is sound according to the school of al-Akhfash, without objection, but Sībawayh refused it, what is the way of explaining the verse according to him? I say: there are two ways according to him. One is that it be by the implication of في, and what makes it fine is that it was mentioned in the two preceding verses, and the reading of Ibn Masʿūd supports it. The second is that آيات is accusative as specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) after the genitive phrase is complete, being conjoined to what precedes, or as repetition, and its nominative is by implying "they are". And «واختلاف الليل والنهار» was also read with nominative."
(تِلْكَ آياتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوها عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ): تلك is the subject and آيات الله the predicate; the clause نتلوها is circumstantial. It is also possible that آيات الله is a substitute for the demonstrative and the clause نتلوها is the predicate; عليك is attached to نتلوها; بالحق is a ḥāl, that is, "bound up with the truth".
(فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ وَآياتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; بأي is attached to يؤمنون; the interrogative is rebuking and means negation, that is, "they do not believe"; حديث is annexed to أي; بعد الله is an adverbial attached to an omitted adjective of الحديث; يؤمنون is a nominative imperfect verb.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «إن في السموات» to His words «يعقلون» there is the art of selection (fann al-takhyīr). It is that the poet or writer brings verses or sentences in which it is permissible to end with various rhymes, and he selects from them a rhyme which he prefers over the rest. Eloquence in the verses requires that the closing (fāṣila) of the first verse be «للمؤمنين», because He, Glory be to Him, mentioned the world in its entirety when He said "the heavens and the earth", and knowing what is in the world of signs indicating that the Originator is Powerful, Knowing and Wise requires first of all affirming the Maker, so that what is in the thing made may be a proof that He is described by those attributes; and the affirmation is belief (īmān). Likewise His word, Exalted, in the second verse «لقوم يوقنون», for the creation of man and the management of the creation of animals and reflecting on that increase him in certainty in his first belief. Likewise knowing the particulars of the world, from the alternation of night and day, the sending down of provision from the heaven, the giving of life to the earth after its death, and the turning about of the winds, calls for soundness of reason, so that he may know that He who made these particulars is the One who made the whole world, once the proof has been established that the whole world has a maker who acts by choice. Therefore eloquence required that the closing of the third verse be «لقوم يعقلون»; and although reason is needed in all of them, mentioning it here is stronger in meaning than in the first.

dervis-irab:7-11.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ): ويل is the subject, and it is a word of punishment, which is why it is permissible to begin with it; ولكل أفاك is its predicate and أثيم an adjective; both are intensive forms for lying and sinning.
(يَسْمَعُ آياتِ اللَّهِ تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ): the clause يسمع is an adjective of أفاك أثيم or a ḥāl from the pronoun in them; you may also make it resumptive. يسمع آيات الله is an imperfect verb, latent agent and direct object; the clause تتلى عليه is a ḥāl of آيات الله; عليه is attached to تتلى.
(ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسْتَكْبِراً كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْها): ثم is a conjunction of sequence and delay; يصر is an imperfect verb conjoined to يسمع. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its origin is from the persistence of the donkey upon the herd of wild asses, which is that it inclines to it pricking its ears (ṣārran udhunayhi)." I say: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "ṣarra al-faras udhunayhi means he pressed them to his head; if they do not use the hamza they say aṣarra al-faras with alif." مستكبرا is a ḥāl from the agent of يصر; كأن is the lightened form of the heavy كأنّ, its noun being the pronoun of the matter, and the clause لم يسمعها its predicate; the sentence is a second ḥāl, that is, "he persists, being like one who does not hear".
(وَإِذا عَلِمَ مِنْ آياتِنا شَيْئاً اتَّخَذَها هُزُواً): the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverbial of the future containing the meaning of condition; the clause علم is in the position of genitive, the adverbial being annexed to it; من آياتنا is attached to علم or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of شيئا; شيئا is the direct object; the clause اتخذها has no position, since it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; the hāʾ is the first object of اتخذ and هزوا the second object of اتخذ.
(أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): the demonstrative is the subject; لهم is a fronted predicate; عذاب is a postponed subject; مهين is an adjective of عذاب; the sentence is the predicate of أولئك, and the sentence of أولئك is resumptive.
(مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ جَهَنَّمُ): من ورائهم is a fronted predicate and جهنم a postponed subject. warāʾ is a noun for the direction which a person is hidden by, whether behind or in front. He said:
أليس ورائي أن تراخت منيتي ... أدبّ مع الولدان أزحف كالنسر
(Is it not ahead of me, if my death be delayed, that I creep along with the children, crawling like the vulture?)
More of this discussion will come in the section of Rhetoric.
(وَلا يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ ما كَسَبُوا شَيْئاً): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يغني is a nominative imperfect verb; عنهم is attached to يغني; ما is a relative, the agent; it may also be a maṣdar particle, in which case the interpreted maṣdar is the agent; شيئا is the direct object.
(وَلا مَا اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِياءَ): conjoined to ما كسبوا; ما may also be relative or maṣdar; من دون الله is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أولياء; أولياء is the second object of اتخذوا, and the first is omitted, that is, "they took them".
(وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; ولهم is a fronted predicate, عذاب a postponed subject, and عظيم an adjective of عذاب.
(هذا هُدىً وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ): a resumptive sentence, introduced to explain the guidance of the Qur'an. هذا is the subject and هدى the predicate; الذين is a subject; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of the relative; بآيات ربهم is attached to كفروا; ولهم is a fronted predicate and عذاب a postponed subject, and the sentence is the predicate of the relative noun; من رجز is an adjective of عذاب, al-rijz being punishment in general; أليم is an adjective of رجز.

* Rhetoric:
Contrariety (al-taḍādd): in His words «من ورائه جهنم» there is contrariety, which is the use of a word that bears a meaning and its opposite, being shared between the two meanings, so that it is used for a thing and its opposite. The verse we cited as evidence in the section of i'rab is by ʿUbayd ibn al-Abraṣ, and the hamza in it is for affirmation (taqrīr). The sense of warāʾ has been widened so that it is used for everything unseen, including the future. أدبّ means "I walk slowly", and the maṣdar particle أن is implied before it because it is the noun of ليس; أزحف may be a substitute for أدبّ, and أن a ḥāl; وكالنسر is also a ḥāl. «[Translator's note: the source text is as written; the sentence "and أن a ḥāl" appears to be slightly garbled.]»

* Benefits:
The return of the pronoun: one of the things hard to understand at first glance is the return of the pronoun in His words «اتخذها هزوا», because the apparent sense of the speech suggests that it returns to "something" (shayʾ), which is masculine; yet he turned from اتخذه to اتخذها, signalling that when he senses that something of the speech is among the verses which Allah sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ, he engages in mockery of all the verses, and does not confine himself to mocking what has reached him of them. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible: 'when he knows of Our verses something that the obstinate one can cling to and find a handle for climbing up to a criticism and a pretext, he seizes the opportunity and takes the verses of Allah as a mockery', like the seizing by Ibn al-Zibaʿrā of His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «إنكم وما تدعون من دون الله حصب جهنم» and his sophistry against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his saying 'I have bested you'. The pronoun may also return to shayʾ because it has the sense of 'verse', as in the saying of Abu al-ʿAtāhiya:
نفسي بشيء من الدنيا معلقة ... الله والقائم المهدي يكفيها
(My soul is attached to something of this world; Allah and the one who stands in charge, al-Mahdī, suffice for it,)
where he meant ʿUtba." Abu al-ʿAtāhiya used "something" as an allusion to a girl among al-Mahdī's favourites called ʿUtba, and so he returned the pronoun to it in the feminine. After it comes:
إني لأيأس منها ثم يطمعني ... فيها احتقارك للدنيا وما فيها
(I despair of her, then your contempt for the world and what is in it gives me hope of her.)
The meaning of the two verses is that he wants nothing from this world except this one thing, and the one who is in charge of the matter suffices for it, that is, suffices me that need or suffices my soul what it desires; and "Allah" is with a cut-off hamza, because the beginning of the hemistich is a place for beginning a sentence. Then: I despair of her and cut off my hope of her, then I hope for her again because of your contempt for the world and what is in it; and this is praise of the utmost generosity. It is related that he wrote this on a garment, rolled it up in a jar and presented it to al-Mahdī; he intended to hand her over to him, but the girl said: "Will you hand me over to a man who earns his living?" So he ordered the jar to be filled with money and gave it to him. He said to the treasurers, "He only ordered dinars for me", and the treasurers said to him, "We will give you dirhams", and they disagreed. She said: "Were he a lover, he would not have distinguished between them."

dervis-irab:12-15.t:
* I'rab:
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْبَحْرَ لِتَجْرِيَ الْفُلْكُ فِيهِ بِأَمْرِهِ): a resumptive sentence, introduced to draw a lesson from the subjection of the sea, in all its vastness, and of the ships running upon it, to a creature who is the tiniest thing in relation to both. الله is the subject and الذي its predicate; the clause سخر is the ṣila; لكم is attached to سخر; البحر is the direct object; the lām is of cause; تجري is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to تجري; الفلك is the agent; بأمره is a ḥāl.
(وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): conjoined to what precedes; لعل with its noun and predicate.
(وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمْ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً مِنْهُ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the sentence is conjoined to its two predecessors; جميعا is a ḥāl of ما. al-Jalāl erred, following Ibn Mālik in his parsing, in that he counted it among the words of emphasis, and so parsed it as emphasis of the relative ما which is the object of سخر; but had that been so, one would have said جميعه, and further, emphasis with jamīʿ is rare, so the Revelation is not to be interpreted by it. منه is a ḥāl, that is, "He subjected them, deriving from Him, Exalted, and coming from Him". al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be attached to an omitted predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "they are all from Him".
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): إن is a particle resembling the verb; وفي ذلك is its fronted predicate; the lām is for emphasis; آيات is the postponed noun of إن; ولقوم is an adjective of آيات; the clause يتفكرون is an adjective of قوم.
(قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَغْفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ لِيَجْزِيَ قَوْماً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): قل is an imperative whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; للذين is attached to قل; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila of the relative and has no position; يغفروا is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to a request, by analogy with condition and apodosis, as in your saying "Stand, you will gain good". It is also said to be by omission of the lām, and also said to be in the sense of "Say to them: forgive, they will forgive", so it is the answer to an omitted command which the speech indicates. A lengthy discussion has already preceded of His word, Exalted, «قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة» in Sūrat Ibrāhīm, so renew your acquaintance with it. وللذين is attached to يغفروا; the clause لا يرجون is the ṣila of the relative; أيام الله is the object. The meaning of "the days of Allah" will come in the section of Benefits. وليجزي: the lām is of cause, and يجزي is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يغفروا, since it is the reason for it; قوما is the direct object; the agent is latent, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah; بما is attached to يجزي; ما may be relative or maṣdar; كان with its noun, and the clause يكسبون is its predicate. The secret of the indefiniteness of قوما will come in the section of Rhetoric.
(مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَساءَ فَعَلَيْها ثُمَّ إِلى رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ): من is conditional, in the position of nominative as the subject; the sentence is resumptive, introduced to explain how recompense occurs; عمل is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, with a latent agent referring to من; صالحا is a direct object or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar.

* Rhetoric:
In His word, Exalted, «ليجزي قوما بما كانوا يكسبون» there is indefiniteness (al-tankīr): He made قوما indefinite although they are known. The narrators and biographers differed about them, which can be consulted in its proper sources. He inclined to indefiniteness only to magnify them and praise them, since by them is meant, on the most preferred opinion, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, as if He had said: "These who restrain themselves and bear harm with patience and steadfastness are a people, and what a people!" This falls under the category of tajrīd (abstraction), which we have presented in detail with its divisions.

* Benefits:
The days of Allah: what is meant by His words «لا يرجون أيام الله» is the famous battles in which truth triumphed over falsehood, and falsehood was brought down by striving. This follows the manner of the Arabs, who say "the days of the Arabs" for their famous battles, as in the words of al-Samawʾal:
وأيامنا مشهورة في عدونا ... لها غرر معلومة وحجول
(Our days are famous against our enemy; they have well-known blazes and white leg-markings.)
And Ẓālim ibn al-Barrāʾ al-Fuqaymī said of the Day of Dhū Bahdā (on the pattern of sukrā):
ونحن غداة يوم ذوات بهدى ... لدى الوتدات إذ غشيت تميم
(And we, on the morning of the Day of Dhawāt Bahdā, at the tent-pegs, when Tamīm was overwhelmed,)
ضربنا الخيل بالأبطال حتى ... تولت وهي شاملها الكلوم
(struck the cavalry with heroes until it turned back, wounds covering it.)
And Jarir said to al-Akhṭal, taunting him with that day:
هل تعرفون بذي بهدى نوار سنا ... يوم الهذيل بأيدي القوم منتشر
(Do you know, at Dhū Bahdā, the blossom of ... the day of al-Hudhayl, in the hands of the people, scattered?) «[Translator's note: the second hemistich of this verse is obscure in the source, and the gloss is tentative.]» Return to al-Aghānī and al-ʿUmda, for in them is a full detail of the days of the Arabs in the pre-Islamic period and in Islam.

dervis-irab:16-21.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ): a resumptive sentence, introduced to inform the Prophet ﷺ that the path on which his people walk is the path on which the nations before them walked. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty; آتينا is a verb and agent; بني إسرائيل is the first direct object; الكتاب is the second direct object; الحكم والنبوة are conjoined to الكتاب.
(وَرَزَقْناهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ وَفَضَّلْناهُمْ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ): ورزقناهم is conjoined to آتينا and is a verb, agent and direct object; من الطيبات is attached to رزقناهم; وفضلناهم على العالمين is conjoined to what precedes. The meaning of the preferment is that no others were given the like of what We gave them.
(وَآتَيْناهُمْ بَيِّناتٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْياً بَيْنَهُمْ): also conjoined; بينات is a second direct object, its sign of accusative being the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; من الأمر is an adjective of بينات, that is, "clear proofs in the matter of religion". فما: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negative; اختلفوا is a verb and agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; من بعد is attached to اختلفوا; ما is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar genitive by annexation; جاءهم العلم is a verb with a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; بغيا is an object of purpose; بينهم is an adverbial attached to an omitted adjective of بغيا.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فِيما كانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ): إن and its noun, with the clause يقضي as its predicate; بينهم is an adverbial attached to يقضي; ويوم القيامة is attached to an omitted ḥāl; فيما is also attached to يقضي; the clause كانوا is the ṣila; the clause يختلفون is the predicate of كان; وفيه is attached to يختلفون.
(ثُمَّ جَعَلْناكَ عَلى شَرِيعَةٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ فَاتَّبِعْها): ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay and the speech is resumptive; جعلناك is a verb, agent and first direct object; وعلى شريعة is in the position of the second object. al-Sharīʿa originally means the waters and rivers to which people come to drink; this was borrowed for religion and worship, because servants come to what gives life to their souls. من الأمر is an adjective of شريعة; the fāʾ is a conjunction; اتبعها is an imperative, agent and direct object.
(وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تتبع is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا; أهواء is the direct object; الذين is a genitive noun in annexation; the clause لا يعلمون is an adjective.
(إِنَّهُمْ لَنْ يُغْنُوا عَنْكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): the sentence has no position, because it gives the reason for the prohibition against following their desires; إن and its noun, with the clause لن يغنوا as its predicate; عنك is attached to يغنوا; من الله is also attached to يغنوا; شيئا is the object.
(وَإِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن and its noun; بعضهم is the subject and أولياء بعض the predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of إن; والله is the subject and ولي المتقين the predicate.
(هذا بَصائِرُ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ): هذا is the subject and بصائر its predicate; the predicate is in the plural in view of what the subject, which is the Qur'an, contains of verses and clear proofs; وللناس is an adjective of بصائر; هدى ورحمة are conjoined to بصائر; ولقوم is an adjective; the clause يوقنون is an adjective of قوم; and the whole sentence is resumptive.
(أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ اجْتَرَحُوا السَّيِّئاتِ أَنْ نَجْعَلَهُمْ كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): أم is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) أم, in the sense of the hamza and "rather" (bal), and the speech is resumptive, introduced to show the difference between the states of the evildoers and the doers of good. حسب is a past verb and الذين its agent; the clause اجترحوا السيئات is the ṣila; أن and what is within its scope are an interpreted maṣdar standing in the place of the two objects of حسب; نجعلهم is an imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "We", the hāʾ the first object of نجعل; and كالذين is in the position of the second object; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; وعملوا الصالحات is conjoined to آمنوا.
(سَواءً مَحْياهُمْ وَمَماتُهُمْ ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ): سواء is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, which are كالذين آمنوا. The meaning is: "Do those who committed evil deeds think that We shall make them like those who believed and did righteous deeds, in a state where their living and their dying are equal?" The interrogative has the sense of denial and negation. محياهم is the agent of سواء; ساء is a past verb of censure, and ما here is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar which is the agent of ساء; or ما is a complete indefinite noun in the sense of "something", in the position of accusative as specification, and the agent of ساء is latent, its implied form being "he".

* Benefits:
1- The weeping place of the worshippers (mabkāt al-ʿābidīn): this verse «أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات» etc. is called the "weeping place of the worshippers". On the authority of Tamīm al-Dārī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was praying one night at the Station (al-Maqām), and when he reached this verse he began to weep and to repeat «ساء ما يحكمون» until morning. And al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ used to say to himself: "Would that I knew which of the two groups you are!"
2- A second reading of the verse: «سواء محياهم ومماتهم» was also read with nominative; then سواء is a fronted predicate and محياهم a postponed subject. There is disagreement about the parsing of this sentence. al-Zamakhsharī said that it is a substitute for the kāf, because the sentence occurs as a second object and so is in the rule of a single word. Abū Ḥayyān replied: "This which al-Zamakhsharī held, the substitution of a sentence for a single word, was permitted by Abu al-Fatḥ and chosen by Ibn Mālik, who adduced for it evidence, in his opinion, in which the substitution is not necessarily the case," until he says: "What appears to me is that if we say the sentence is attached to what precedes, the sentence is in the position of ḥāl, and the implied form is: 'Do the disbelievers think that their destiny is like that of the believers, in a state where their living and dying are equal? They are not so, but are separated, how wide a separation, in both states.' And this ḥāl clarifies what was left vague in the likeness indicated by the kāf, which is in the position of the second object.'"
